checks.label: Where gears meet, the teeth of both move the same way, so the gears turn opposite ways: true at every mesh that turns, on every screen
An odd number of gears in a closed loop in a plane will not turn, whatever their size and tooth count: every odd loop drawn locks, every even one turns, and an odd loop of mixed sizes locks too
When gear 1 and gear 2 are in mesh, N1 × Z1 = N2 × Z2: speed × teeth is the same on both sides of every mesh drawn with speeds, so the idler screen shows 60, 36 and 20 rev/min

Both counters at a mesh always match: two turns of the 12-tooth driver pass 24 teeth on each side, three turns pass 36 and turn the 36-tooth gear once, and the idler passes on the same count at both its meshes

Each mesh flips the direction: the 20-tooth gear turns against the driver, the fifth of five in a line turns the driver's way, the fourth of four and the sixth of a bent chain the other way, every row follows odd and even, only the loop of six turns, and a fifth gear locks the ring
Each typed answer and slip is worked from speed × teeth: 20 rev/min (slips 180 and 3), 400 rev/min (450 and 3600), 360 rev/min (5760 and 4) and 72 teeth (8), and the board draws the same
Before an answer nothing gives it away: an unknown speed reads "?", the idler's speed and the new gear stay hidden, and only the drivers show their way round; after it, the answer is drawn
Every mesh is drawn with its gears touching at their pitch circles, every loop closes tooth in gap, and gears that do not mesh never touch
Every demonstration is over within 4.5 s of its screen opening and nothing moves during the 0.35 s screen fade; every answer's motion is over within 2.5 s
